subject.title: Swarm: legacy per-session child cap (5) preempts tools.swarm group caps

question: For enabled Swarm collector runs, should collector admission be owned solely by `tools.swarm` group caps, should the legacy per-session child cap be raised, or should both limits intentionally apply?
rationale: The report identifies a conflict between a documented Swarm-cap intent and an existing legacy safety limit; selecting the compatibility and resource-control contract requires maintainer product ownership.

options.title: Make Swarm caps authoritative
options.body: Exempt enabled, host-registered collector children from the legacy per-session cap and enforce `maxConcurrent`, `maxChildrenPerGroup`, and total-group limits as the collector admission contract.

options.title: Raise the legacy cap
options.body: Keep both enforcement layers but increase the per-session limit when Swarm is enabled, accepting two coordinated controls.

options.title: Retain and document both caps
options.body: Keep the legacy cap as an intentional outer guard and document that it can preempt Swarm group settings.

recommendation.title: Make Swarm caps authoritative
recommendation.body: Exempt enabled, host-registered collector children from the legacy per-session cap and enforce `maxConcurrent`, `maxChildrenPerGroup`, and total-group limits as the collector admission contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history context ties this person to the original Swarm specification, live validation, and the most recent adjacent collector-launch repair.
